# Base image with Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support for ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, certificates, and clean up
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a temporary directory for building the application
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the latest version of LAMMPS, build with REAXFF package, and install
# The C and CXX compilers are explicitly set to the MPI wrappers provided by the base image
# to ensure it is built for a multi-node MPI environment.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
        -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
        -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=ON \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
        ../cmake && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the example files for the reaxff HNS benchmark into the working directory
RUN cp /build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /build

# Verify that the LAMMPS executable is in the system PATH
RUN which lmp

RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git && \
    cd lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
        -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \

# MiniCluster manifest for running a LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation on AWS CPU instances.
# This configuration is designed for a multi-node execution environment using ARM architecture.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster set, running across up to 4 nodes.
  size: 4

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job. Flux will execute `flux run -n 4 ...`.
  tasks: 4

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for Flux, required for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible Flux view image.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disable the flux-view sidecar container. Flux daemons will run in the main application container.
      disable: true

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict logging; the job will fail on any error.
    strict: true

  # Prevents the job's pods and services from being deleted after completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Definition of the application container. Only one container is permitted.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by Flux. Do not include 'flux run' or 'mpirun'.
      # This runs a LAMMPS simulation using the specified input file.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container is a worker, not the main job launcher. This MUST be false.
      launcher: false

      # Ensures the latest version of the container image is always used.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This is necessary for high-performance networking on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 24 -v y 12 -v z 12 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
    optionFlags: -o cpu-affinity=per-task
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST parse a result to include the units for katom or Matom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
You MUST set flux.optionFlags to "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
You can use lmp -v x 24 -v y 12 -v z 12 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite to start on 4 nodes (FOM of 2.094 Matom)
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
